In addition, through collaboration with all stakeholders, we are advancing financial inclusion, enhancing the public's financial literacy, and raising awareness of fraud prevention, thereby contributing to the creation of a caring society. The climate challenge is immense and urgently pressing. Economies worldwide are moving toward a more sustainable future, a transition expected to bring profound changes to financing activities and asset allocation. This transformation carries significant latent risks, yet it will also be accompanied by unprecedented opportunities. As a global hub for sustainable finance, Hong Kong has a responsibility to take the lead in addressing these challenges. At the same time, we are well-positioned to build on this momentum. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will fully support the industry in providing financing for the low-carbon transition. As a responsible investor and sustainable institution, it will lead by example and collaborate with like-minded partners to advance this critically important global agenda. President Yu Weiwen.

Climate change risks and other sustainability issues are global in nature. The objectives of the Monetary Authority's sustainability work are to leverage its policies and operations to provide leadership, ensuring that Hong Kong's financial system and the Authority itself are resilient to climate-related risks and are able to support the transition to a more sustainable economy. Through active engagement with international and regional organizations, the HKMA will also strive to participate in the formulation of green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will further enhance the banking sector's climate response capabilities and climate risk management. Specifically, the priority tasks include: launching a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices, accompanied by a new series of consultation meetings, as part of the assessment of banks' progress in implementing regulatory requirements on climate risk management; continuing work on integrating climate factors into the regulatory review processes of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority; completing the second industry-wide climate risk stress test, while providing guidance to participating banks throughout the process and sharing insights and lessons learned with the industry; strengthening sustainability disclosures by collaborating with local authorities to align relevant regulations with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards, which serve as the global benchmark, and preparing for the implementation of the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's Third Pillar 1 framework on climate-related financial risks; and sharing best-practice guidance on transition planning with the industry. To foster the healthy development of banks in providing green and sustainable investment products, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) will continue to closely monitor local and international market and regulatory developments, maintain engagement with the industry, and ensure that banks adopt appropriate sales practices. In addition, the HKMA will also act as a catalyst, striving to foster the development of the green finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for economic transformation. We are soon to launch our local Green Classification Catalogue and will continue to expand its scope to encompass a broader range of activities, including transition activities. At the same time, we will continue to explore the application of technological solutions to assist banks in identifying, measuring, and monitoring their climate-related risk exposures. One such example is the upcoming cloud-based platform, which will enhance banks' assessment of physical climate risks. To enhance the professional competencies of our practitioners, we will also establish the Professional Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Banking Qualifications Framework in 2024. Hong Kong possesses the optimal conditions to serve as a regional and international hub for sustainable finance. To fulfill this role, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) is assisting the Government in implementing the recommendations set out in the 2023–24 Budget to expand the scope of the Government Green Bond Programme (GGBP) to include sustainable finance projects, thereby deepening the development of the local green and sustainable bond market. At the same time, the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme is being leveraged to attract more green financing activities, including transition finance activities, to Hong Kong. We will continue to encourage more government bodies, organizations, and enterprises to raise green funds through Hong Kong, while exploring the potential synergies between green finance and technology. In addition, we will continue to support the implementation of the government-funded Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme to expand Hong Kong's talent pool in green finance. As Co-Chairs of the Cross-Sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance, we will continue to work closely with other relevant institutions to coordinate cross-sectoral policies and initiatives aimed at advancing Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance development. In 2024, the Steering Group will prioritize its work across three key areas: sustainable disclosure, the application of technology, and transition finance. As another key priority, through the Green Banking Alliance, the HKMA and the International Finance Corporation (IFC) will continue to jointly launch targeted initiatives across Asia. These include conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, delivering tailored professional training for banks, and offering practical guidance to support financial institutions in developing their distinctive green transition pathways. In 2024, we will also strive to deepen our collaboration with the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), the Capacity Building for Sustainable Investment (CBSI) Alliance, and the Partnership on Green Development and Investment. As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (HKMA) has committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier. We will continue to enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a responsible investment approach that combines three key pillars, ensuring portfolio resilience as we advance toward net zero. We fully recognize that achieving the objectives of the Paris Agreement requires a comprehensive economic transformation. Accordingly, we are refining our net-zero strategy to prioritize assets that deliver tangible climate benefits to the real economy, while ensuring alignment with the investment objectives of the Exchange Fund. As an environmental advocate, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to evolve its decarbonization strategy to reflect the latest developments in the market, regulation, technology, and other climate-related areas. To further strengthen the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's climate resilience and risk preparedness, we will explore the feasibility of leveraging technology solutions to assess the impact of physical risks on our offices. In addition, we will continue to actively encourage employees to participate in our sustainability initiatives, including launching awareness campaigns to foster sustainable habits and optimizing office processes and practices. In addition, the HKMA will continue to maintain a consistent, efficient, and sustainable procurement approach, including assessing suppliers' ESG practices during the selection and renewal of contracts. Building on its achievement of Green Data Centre certification in 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has committed to upholding the specified certification standards. Regarding the regular upgrades of data center facilities, we not only stay abreast of the latest technological advancements but also incorporate green design principles and sustainable operational practices. At the same time, we will continue to leverage technology and convergence to reduce electronic waste, while proactively modernizing our internal systems to enhance efficiency and minimize potential risks as much as possible. Finally, in the area of community engagement, the Monetary Authority will seek to provide staff with more opportunities for community service and collaborate with industry partners to promote financial inclusion, enhance financial literacy, and raise public awareness of fraud prevention.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its effects. Through its multiple roles as central bank, banking regulator, market enabler, responsible investor, and sustainable development institution, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong contributes to advancing and accelerating the transition to net zero emissions in Hong Kong and across the broader Asia region. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has established a robust sustainable development governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of related measures, and ensure that MAS's own operations and working methods integrate sustainability considerations. To uphold sound corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework characterized by clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. The governance framework ensures that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's strategic planning and decision-making processes effectively incorporate sustainability factors, and establishes robust mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC) and its related sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its sustainable development initiatives, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, which leads the HKMA's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO), responsible for coordinating and supervising ESG-related activities within the EFIO in the area of responsible investment; and various task forces and working groups covering other functional areas, tasked with planning and implementing relevant sustainable development measures across banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sector level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Agency Coordinating Group (the Coordinating Group), jointly established by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other relevant parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. Given the significant expansion of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) sustainable development initiatives over the past few years, we established a Steering Committee in October to serve as a new central platform for leading and more effectively coordinating all sustainable development activities across the HKMA's various functional areas. Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans concerning ESG matters across the four functional areas of banking, market development, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations; oversee the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's functional departments; assess the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and monitor external communication strategies. The Supervisory Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong, with its three Deputy Chief Executives serving as ex officio members. Additionally, we will invite Assistant Presidents in charge of key functions related to green initiatives and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on their major achievements and future plans. The Supervisory Committee convenes regular meetings, supported by relevant working groups under the Banking Division, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to formulating and implementing their own sustainable development initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly established the Supervisory Task Force in May 2020. The Steering Group, serving as a cross-agency platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sector efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby reinforcing Hong Kong's position as a leading global and Asian hub for green and sustainable finance. For detailed information on the Working Group's activities, please refer to the chapter titled "Strengthening the Ecosystem for Green and Sustainable Finance."

Climate change represents a significant risk to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) remains committed to strengthening Hong Kong's financial system to build a greener and more sustainable future, contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face a range of sustainability and climate-related issues in their daily operations. To continue fulfilling their vital role within the financial system and channel more capital toward green and sustainable projects, banks must proactively manage climate-related risks. As the banking regulator, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has focused on strengthening banks' capacity to address and manage climate risks, while accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. The Monetary Authority is committed to formulating diverse policy measures to enhance the banking sector's capacity to address climate-related risks. In August, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority issued a notification on Net Zero Transition Planning, setting out high-level principles to assist banks in maintaining safety and soundness as the economy transitions toward net-zero emissions. Following the issuance of that circular, we conducted a questionnaire survey in the fourth quarter with selected banks to understand their transformation planning measures. Based on the survey findings, we will share insights and best practices regarding transformation planning with the industry, and will organize seminars and workshops to facilitate experience exchange among industry practitioners. In the area of disclosure requirements, in light of recent international developments—including the International Sustainability Disclosure Standards released in June and the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision's (BCBS) November consultation on its third pillar disclosure framework for climate-related financial risks—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is strengthening its efforts to enhance the sustainability-related disclosure framework for Hong Kong banks. Specifically, the HKMA is working with local authorities and stakeholders to develop a comprehensive roadmap for Hong Kong aligned with the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) Sustainability Disclosure Standards. Within the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority strengthened its regulatory oversight of banks' climate risk management and provided recommendations to help banks further enhance their climate response capabilities and climate risk management frameworks. The Monetary Authority of Singapore has made significant progress in implementing its two-year plan to incorporate climate risk factors into the banking regulatory framework. Climate risk management has now been established as a standing agenda item for prudential regulatory meetings held with bank management. Banking regulators also employ an enhanced CAMEL rating framework that incorporates climate risk factors to assess banks' risk profiles and risk management systems. As part of implementing a two-year plan to integrate climate risk factors into the banking regulatory framework, the Monetary Authority has revised its "green" assessment framework to focus on banks' transition planning measures. The HKMA is also reviewing the regulatory examination procedures used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements, with a view to encouraging banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks in addressing climate-related risks. Following the conclusion of the 12-month implementation period for Compliance with Section GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Regulatory Policy Manual under the 2023 two-year plan, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority launched a thematic review on climate-related risk governance in the second quarter. The thematic review covers four key areas: governance frameworks for climate-related risks, oversight of climate strategy, oversight of climate-related risk management, and organizational culture, awareness, and communication. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has implemented several enhancements to its climate risk stress testing framework, including the introduction of new five-year scenarios to assess the potential impact on banks from the simultaneous occurrence of economic and climate change shocks. Following the implementation of these enhancements and as part of the HKMA's regular regulator-led stress testing programme, the second round of climate risk stress tests commenced in June to comprehensively assess banks' climate risk exposures and further strengthen their capacity to manage climate-related risks. Forty-four banks participated in this risk stress test, representing an increase of over 60% compared to the inaugural pilot program in 2021. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAH) also hosted a climate risk stress testing forum in November, which attracted up to 300 banking professionals. By fostering the exchange of experience among banks, this initiative has helped deepen the industry's overall understanding of climate risk measurement. The HKMA also held a series of consultation meetings to review the progress made by banks in implementing the HKMA's Supervisory Policy Manual module GS-1, "Climate Risk Management." The Hong Kong Monetary Authority held a meeting with bank management to discuss their work on climate risk management and the shared challenges facing the industry, and to review data provided by the banks and other publicly available information in order to assess progress. The HKMA provides targeted advice to banks, encouraging and supporting them to further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities in line with the HKMA's regulatory expectations. Amid growing global concern over climate change and concerted efforts to address the issue, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has observed a rising demand for green and sustainable investment products, with some banks introducing such offerings to meet customer needs. In light of this, the HKMA completed a thematic review of banks' sales of green and sustainable investment products and issued an announcement in November setting out the standards expected of banks and sharing observed good practices. This notice covers multiple areas, including product due diligence, disclosure, governance and control measures, staff training, and record-keeping. It aims to mitigate potential greenwashing risks and bolster investor confidence, thereby fostering the sound development of relevant investment activities. The Monetary Authority will continue to monitor emerging trends and market developments. The Monetary Authority of Singapore is committed to promoting the application of technology in green and sustainable banking. For instance, technology can enhance data availability and risk analysis, thereby strengthening banks' capacity to manage climate-related risks. The Monetary Authority will soon launch a pilot cloud-based platform to enable banks to assess the impact of physical climate risks on residential and commercial buildings under various climate scenarios. In addition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore continues to collaborate with other central banks and regulatory authorities to explore how technology solutions can assist in assessing physical risks. On the other hand, the HKMA also encourages the adoption of sustainable anti-money laundering (AML) practices by leveraging advanced analytics and artificial intelligence to reduce the consumption of compliance-related resources. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched an online shared data submission platform to fully automate the collection of financial crime risk data, thereby enhancing banks' operational processes for submitting anti-money laundering (AML) data in a sustainable manner. In September, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched the "Green Fintech Competition" to identify market-ready solutions that assist the banking sector in addressing challenges across the following areas: (i) net-zero transition or transition planning; (ii) climate risk management; (iii) green and sustainable finance; and (iv) sustainability or climate-related disclosure and reporting. The competition attracted over 85 submissions from approximately 70 companies. In December, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) hosted the "Green and Sustainable Banking Symposium," providing a platform for the banking and technology sectors to discuss the role of low-carbon technologies and green fintech in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and mainland China. The event also announced the results of the "Green Fintech Competition." The event attracted approximately 400 participants from banks, technology companies, regulatory bodies, and academia. To enhance transparency across financial markets and foster greater alignment in green and sustainable finance decisions, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, with the assistance of a consulting firm, has developed a local green taxonomy framework. In May, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) issued a consultation paper on the prototype of the Hong Kong Green Taxonomy, seeking stakeholders' views on the development and implementation of a green classification directory. Based on the consultation outcomes, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is refining the framework prototype and identifying additional components for the next phase of framework development. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority participates in the work of the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), which has recognized environmental crimes as predicate offences for money laundering. In light of the interconnection between anti-money laundering and environmental, social, and governance (ESG) considerations, this area is attracting increasing attention from regulators. The Monetary Authority recognizes that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; accordingly, it has expanded its financial risk analysis and research to incorporate a broader range of climate factors and scenarios, thereby strengthening its current oversight. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the Monetary Authority will take climate change into account and incorporate analyses of climate-related risks into its financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has helped further enrich climate scenarios, enabling central banks and regulators to better understand the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial system. As a member of the Transition Planning Task Force under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA has contributed to analyzing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to adopt a forward-looking and dynamic perspective on climate-related financial risks. In terms of research, the HKMA has undertaken several applied research projects to examine the impact of climate change and broader ESG issues on the financial sector and the economy. Research topics include the financial sector's exposure to climate risks, ESG capital flows, the impact of climate change on property prices, and the ripple effects of corporate ESG performance across global supply chains. The aforementioned research findings have enhanced the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's understanding of the impact of climate change and ESG issues on financial stability, thereby aiding in the formulation of relevant policies. Locally, these studies will enhance the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate risks on financial stability. Externally, the HKMA disseminates research findings to a broad range of stakeholders through international activities on climate-related matters and various channels, including the HKMA Research Memorandum. The Monetary Authority of Singapore's "Liquidity Facility Framework" is a collateralized standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has, in line with NGFS recommendations, incorporated sustainability considerations into the assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is actively engaged in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and advancing sustainable finance as a mainstream priority. Through its engagement in this area, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority helps foster international and regional policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability, while drawing on insights to strengthen the climate resilience of Hong Kong's financial system.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading hub for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and catalysts, and supporting international initiatives to align with global standards. Over the past year, the HKMA has worked closely with local and international partners to build a richer ecosystem and advance the further development of Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance sector. The Cross-sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group), jointly led by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the financial sector's response to climate and environmental risks, accelerating the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong, and supporting the Government's climate strategy. The supervisory group has made significant progress since its establishment. In January 2024, the Steering Committee unveiled key measures to support Hong Kong in seizing opportunities in sustainable finance. The main areas of focus include sustainable disclosure, strengthening the ecosystem, transition finance, and green fintech. Specifically, the Sustainability Disclosure Working Group has been established to develop a roadmap for Hong Kong's adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards. The roadmap will encompass four key areas: sustainable reporting, assurance, data and technology, and skills training. Additionally, a Transition Finance Working Group has been established to explore methods for supporting financial institutions and enterprises in their transition planning and reporting. The Steering Committee has also strengthened the development of a sustainable finance ecosystem through cross-sector skills training and data enhancement. In particular regarding data, we continue to advance the adoption of Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Private Companies 2, which was launched in collaboration with CDP by the Supervisory Group in 2022. The Steering Group will continue to closely monitor the latest developments in green and sustainable finance and enhance Hong Kong's position as a regional and global hub for green and sustainable finance. In January 2024, the Steering Group announced three new key initiatives to capitalize on investment and financing opportunities arising from low-carbon transition in the Asia-Pacific region. To support industry skills development, the Green and Sustainable Finance Centre under the Supervisory Committee has implemented the government's "Green and Sustainable Finance Training Pilot Scheme," providing funding to practitioners, students, and graduates who undergo relevant training and obtain qualifications in green and sustainable finance. As of December 2023, a total of 46 international and local training programs and qualifications had been registered as eligible under the scheme, and over 560 subsidy applications had been approved. The Monetary Authority has also launched the foundational level of the new "Green and Sustainable Finance" module under the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework. This unit aims to foster talent development in the banking sector and enhance the overall professional capabilities of practitioners. In 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to collaborate with the banking industry to establish professional standards for this unit, addressing the rapidly growing demand for professionals in green and sustainable finance. To enhance the understanding of financial institutions and enterprises, particularly small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), on key climate and sustainability-related issues—including climate risk management, sustainability reporting, greenhouse gas emissions accounting, and transition planning—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) collaborated this year with relevant government policy bureaux and departments, as well as global partners such as CDP, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ), and the Partnership for Carbon Accounting Financials (PCAF). Through a series of seminars and specialized workshops, the HKMA engaged professionals from the financial services and corporate sectors. On the student front, following the launch of the Sustainable Finance Internship Programme in 2022, training courses were held in January and February 2023 to enhance the understanding of sustainable finance among interns and graduates of bachelor's degree programmes. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority recognizes the potential of technology in addressing climate-related data gaps and enhancing data quality. Accordingly, it is committed to making such data more accessible and improving their quality to support informed decision-making and effective climate action. In February 2024, the Steering Committee launched a series of website enhancements to provide financial institutions, businesses, and the public with a one-stop platform for green and sustainable finance information. Key enhancements include the sustainable disclosure e-platform, greenhouse gas emission calculation and estimation tools, and more centralized, user-friendly, and searchable data and resources. During Hong Kong Green Week, the Steering Committee, in collaboration with Hong Kong Science Park and the Investment Promotion Department, co-hosted the event "Leveraging Technology to Catalyze Sustainable Finance," showcasing leading green innovation solutions and Hong Kong's competitive advantages in green technology. The Hong Kong Green Week – Financial Theme, held from February 26 to March 1, 2024, featured a series of sustainability-focused events that attracted over 1,600 participants from nearly 30 regions, including representatives from financial institutions, corporations, central banks, international organizations, government agencies, academia, and consulting firms. The flagship event of the Hong Kong Green Week is the Asia-Pacific Climate Business Forum, co-hosted by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority and the International Finance Corporation. The forum brought together over 400 guests, including top decision-makers from the global business and finance sectors, to discuss strategies for unlocking climate finance in the Asia-Pacific region. This two-day event explored a broad range of topics, including energy transition, decarbonization of heavy industry, the circular economy, the future of sustainable finance, and emerging climate technologies in developing and emerging markets across the Asia-Pacific region. The forum has garnered support from both public and private sectors, jointly organizing over 10 roundtable discussions, seminars, and other exchange activities. The agenda covers climate finance, carbon markets, electric vehicle supply chains, financing for net-zero transition, green finance taxonomies, and green development financing in the Belt and Road region. Furthermore, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) co-hosted the "Asia Climate Finance Roundtable" with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) on February 29, 2024, to discuss key measures for scaling up climate finance and the roles of central banks and regulators in climate risk management. The aforementioned activities form part of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) broader efforts to foster and enrich Hong Kong's green and sustainable finance ecosystem. They serve as a valuable platform for participants to advance new business development, share knowledge, and explore emerging opportunities to address climate finance challenges across the Asia-Pacific region. The Monetary Authority of Singapore has also been actively supporting the development of green and sustainable finance within the region. In November 2020, the International Finance Corporation (IFC) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) launched the Green Commercial Banking Alliance, a collaborative platform bringing together regional financial institutions, banking industry associations, research organizations, and technology innovators to jointly advance the development of green commercial banking. Since March 2021, the Alliance has organized 22 training sessions and roundtable meetings, engaging more than 7,300 participants from across the globe, including the Asia-Pacific region, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Americas. In October, the Alliance, in collaboration with Crédit Agricole CIB, released its second flagship research report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: Case Studies." In October, the Alliance and Crédit Agricole CIB jointly released the frontiers research report titled "Developing an Ambitious Green Banking Climate Strategy: Case Studies." Within the year, the Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office of the Monetary Authority of Macao joined the newly established Sustainable Investment Capacity Building Alliance (CASI) and the Green Investment and Financing Partnership (GIFP) initiated by the Belt and Road International Alliance for Green Development. The collaboration with CASI and GIFP will enhance capacity building and facilitate knowledge sharing, while also directing additional funding toward green and sustainable projects across Asia and beyond. In August 2023, the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) announced the establishment of its Hong Kong chapter, which will help support net-zero transition efforts by financial institutions in Hong Kong and mainland China. The Monetary Authority assists GFANZ in its work in an advisory capacity. To demonstrate the Government's resolve in addressing climate change, promoting green finance, and fostering Hong Kong's development into a more sustainable and livable city, the Government launched the Green Bond Programme in 2018. The Monetary Authority of Singapore assists in the issuance of green bonds under the initiative. To date, the Government has issued approximately $25 billion in green institutional and retail bonds. The proceeds have been allocated to over 70 green government projects, including green buildings, waste management and resource recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. To enhance the transparency and accountability of the programme, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report, which details the allocation of funds raised through green bonds and their anticipated environmental benefits. In the 2023-24 fiscal year, the Government continued its regular issuance of green government bonds, issuing approximately USD 6 billion worth of green bonds in June. This tri-currency issuance, featuring bonds denominated in US dollars, euros, and renminbi across various maturities, attracted a diverse range of investors. The subscription response was robust, with total subscribed amounts reaching nearly USD 30 billion. The issuance of RMB bonds increased from 10 billion yuan in January to 15 billion yuan, and for the first time, 10-year RMB bonds were introduced. This move will help extend the government's RMB yield curve and further diversify the range of offshore RMB products available. Global investors have responded enthusiastically to the issuance of green bonds by the government, reflecting their affirmation of Hong Kong's commitment to promoting green and sustainable development. In October, the Government issued the second tranche of green retail bonds totaling HK$20 billion, further advancing market development and promoting inclusive finance. This issuance offers the public a stable-return investment opportunity, enabling them to participate in and benefit from the development of green finance in Hong Kong.

As a significant global owner and manager of assets, the Monetary Authority of Singapore plays a pivotal role in advancing green and sustainable finance to support the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority of Singapore has long been a pioneer in responsible investment. Since 2015, the Monetary Authority has spearheaded green and sustainable asset investment by requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise ownership rights and integrate environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors into the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. In line with the principle of "prioritizing capital preservation and pursuing long-term value appreciation," the Monetary Authority of Singapore invests prudently, believing that giving full attention to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors helps mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As one of the first central banks to sign the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI) and to set a "net-zero by 2050" target for its portfolio, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong is committed to advancing its responsible investment journey, with a strong emphasis on sustainability, particularly the urgent challenge of climate change. This effort aims to enhance the resilience of the Exchange Fund and secure improved risk-adjusted long-term returns. As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority contributes to building a robust green and sustainable finance ecosystem by collaborating with like-minded investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations to establish industry-wide operational standards, and by promoting the adoption of responsible investment practices across the financial sector and central banking community. Through supervisory and collaborative measures, the HKMA is committed to fostering a future where financial stability and sustainable development advance in tandem. Figure 1: A comprehensive and reliable flow of ESG information is essential to the Exchange Fund's responsible investment journey, enabling the integration of sustainability and the planning of a credible climate transition to achieve net-zero targets. In fulfillment of its commitment to the NGFS Glasgow Declaration and the Cross-Industry Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance Strategy Plan, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong has taken the lead by preparing this chapter on the responsible investment of the Exchange Fund, in line with the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD). The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established a responsible investment framework and guiding principles, which are implemented by the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund in the management of the Fund's investments. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for the Exchange Fund's approach to balancing responsible investment practices with its investment objectives. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the Responsible Investment Framework and risk management policies and monitors their implementation through regular reporting by the Sustainable Investment Group of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund is chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer and is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Investment Office's ESG initiatives. The motions and progress updates discussed by the ESG Committee at its quarterly meetings are reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) and attended by the Chief Executive and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO), convenes biannually to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across various MAHK functions, including those of the EFIO, in order to advance the MAHK's overall ESG objectives. Figure 2 illustrates the Responsible Investment Governance Framework of the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund, as shown in Figure 1. The Investment Office launched its responsible investment journey in 2016, initially focusing on managing ESG risks that could impact the Exchange Fund's financial performance. As sustainability evolves rapidly and moves beyond risk considerations to become a top strategic priority for major institutions worldwide, the Exchange Fund Investment Office has reviewed its responsible investment approach. July 2023 marked another milestone with the establishment of a new Business Strategy Department within the Exchange Fund Investment Office, led by the Chief Strategy Officer. This department is tasked with coordinating and leading the strategic development of the Exchange Fund Investment Office and has incorporated the former Responsible Investment Task Force, originally under the Risk Management and Supervision Department, now rebranded as the Sustainable Investment Team. This strategic adjustment reflects the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's shift in its focus on responsible investment from a risk-based approach to a more proactive and forward-looking stance in addressing investment matters related to sustainable development. The Sustainable Investment Group collaborates closely with the Exchange Fund Investment Office's (EFIO) other teams to integrate ESG factors and assists EFIO senior management in overseeing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment portfolios. For public market investments, the Credit, Regulatory and Oversight Committee, comprising EFIO senior executives, reviews how ESG factors have been incorporated into credit risk models based on the Sustainable Investment Group's recommendations. Additionally, the Risk Management and Monitoring Department provides regular reports to monitor the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Group participates in the selection, appointment, and monitoring of external equity portfolio managers from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 40). Private market investment – The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority, will consider private market investments and the ESG-related assessments provided by the Risk Management team for each investment proposal. The Monetary Authority acknowledges that the physical and transition risks, along with associated opportunities, posed by climate change will affect the long-term performance and value of Exchange Fund investment portfolios. The UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report 2023 projects that, unless greenhouse gas emissions are further reduced globally, the world's average temperature will rise by 2.5 to 2.9°C above pre-industrial levels before 2030. The urgent need for more aggressive policies, technological innovation, or behavioral changes to limit global warming may exacerbate transition risks, including asset stranding and asset depreciation. At the same time, extreme weather events are becoming increasingly frequent and severe, also posing additional physical risks to investment projects. The Monetary Authority believes that investing in a greener future aligns with the Exchange Fund's investment objectives, and therefore places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The Monetary Authority of Singapore's 2022 decision to set a target for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier further underscores its commitment to the global climate agenda. The Monetary Authority continues to strengthen its three-pronged approach, with a clear focus on decarbonization and transition. The following sections will elaborate in detail on the relevant methods. Figure 3: The HKMA's three-pronged approach to responsible investing. In the journey toward net zero, the HKMA prefers to engage proactively rather than exclude or divest from its investable universe. First, maintaining a diversified and robust portfolio is critical to achieving the Exchange Fund's primary investment objective. Directly excluding certain sectors or industries would narrow the investable universe, potentially impacting investment returns and risk profiles. Through a phased approach, the HKMA can seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation that possess advanced technological capabilities and robust corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission sectors. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Simply excluding relevant investment projects or divesting is insufficient to address carbon emissions. In contrast, the Monetary Authority has supported these sectors by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising its ownership rights, thereby driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operational practices and generating beneficial outcomes for itself and the global community. In response to market developments, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is refining its net-zero investment strategy to achieve transformational outcomes that align with the Exchange Fund's objectives and global net-zero goals, while upholding its guiding principles of responsible investment. The Monetary Authority continues to pursue sustainable investment opportunities by integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, thereby advancing climate transition and enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio (Figure 4). The HKMA's Responsible Investment initiative maintained strong momentum in 2023. In the open market, the Monetary Authority launched a new active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, managed by an external investment manager. It also expanded the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to another asset portfolio managed by an external investment manager. Furthermore, the strong performance of green, social, and sustainable development bonds prioritized by the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong, which has outperformed its investment benchmark, demonstrates the principle that doing good and generating profit can go hand in hand. In the private markets, the Monetary Authority is actively building a resilient long-term growth portfolio to capture investment opportunities expected to benefit from long-term economic trends such as climate and energy transition. For instance, within the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) invested in two Asia-focused transition investment funds, demonstrating its commitment to addressing Asia's climate transition needs. Figure 4: Continued Measures to Promote ESG Investing – The Monetary Authority has invested in a company that specializes in producing eco-friendly thermoplastic materials from unsorted household waste (including organic matter such as food scraps) and non-recyclable materials. Unlike traditional chemical recycling systems that rely on high-energy, high-temperature conditions for plastic production, this company has pioneered a low-temperature manufacturing process powered entirely by solar arrays. This plastic material, produced entirely from waste, offers a sustainable and versatile alternative to oil-based resins commonly used in industries such as retail and durable consumer goods. At the same time, this plastic material is compatible with existing standard manufacturing processes and cutting-edge technologies such as 3D printing. The company is firmly committed to the circular economy. In 2017 and 2019, the Monetary Authority of China (MAC) made two separate $1 billion investments in the MCPP commitment. It further partnered with the International Finance Corporation (IFC) to launch the new global climate-related investment platform "MCPP One Planet" in 2021. This platform is the world's first cross-sector emerging market loan portfolio aligned with the Paris Agreement. Through the MCPP initiative, the HKMA has pledged loans to 80 sustainable development projects across 38 developing countries, spanning 19 sectors including infrastructure, agriculture, real estate, and manufacturing. The International Finance Corporation collected data on MCPP loans. According to the International Finance Corporation's report, the Monetary Authority of Singapore's loan commitments have provided support to emerging markets and developing countries in various areas, including economic transformation and human resource development. Specifically, the projects for which the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) provides loans are projected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by approximately 5.6 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent annually, equivalent to the emissions generated by a typical petrol-powered car traveling 14 billion miles. A green and sustainable finance ecosystem is the cornerstone of future global sustainable development. The Monetary Authority of Singapore actively collaborates with like-minded investors and partners to advance responsible investment and enhance industry capabilities.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is committed to becoming a sustainable institution by pursuing a multi-pronged approach to reduce its carbon footprint, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier. In addition to advancing environmental sustainability, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also prioritizes the physical and mental well-being of its staff and upholds social responsibility, while striving to promote financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy. As a responsible institution, the Monetary Authority has established sustainable development goals under three pillars: environment, employees, and social responsibility. Established in October, the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of the Monetary Authority, serves as the primary decision-making body for all institutional sustainable development initiatives. The predecessor of the Steering Committee was the Institutional Social Responsibility and Sustainability Committee, which was responsible for guiding the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in formulating the vision, strategy, and policies for institutional sustainability and social responsibility. At the departmental level, the Assistant President (Corporate Expansion and Operations) oversees the implementation of sustainability initiatives and submits regular progress reports to the Steering Committee. The Green Office Working Group and the Volunteer Service Group support the organization in its sustainable development initiatives. The former serves as a platform for discussing how to create a green workplace, fostering collective brainstorming, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of volunteerism among participants. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has established a roadmap to guide its transformation journey. The core focus lies in implementing decarbonization strategies within daily operations, including operating green buildings and data centers, promoting green mobility, adopting energy-saving measures, leveraging digital tools and more environmentally friendly operational models, reducing waste, and fostering a culture of sustainability. The Monetary Authority of Singapore also plans to leverage carbon-embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions, while employing carbon offset measures for emissions that are difficult to abate. In addition to its environmental commitments related to day-to-day operations, the Monetary Authority continues to introduce more eco-friendly operational initiatives for the wider community, covering channels for banks to submit electronic documents and communicate, as well as electronic payment services and coin collection programs available to the general public. To strengthen and sustain its operational capabilities, the HKMA has engaged a professional team, established a talent pool, and prioritized the physical and mental well-being of its staff. In terms of social responsibility, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) encourages staff to participate in volunteer and charitable activities; in procurement, it considers engaging social enterprises; it promotes financial literacy for consumers; and it collaborates with the banking sector to ensure equitable access to basic banking services for all segments of society. The remainder of this chapter details the strategies outlined above. Within the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) overarching institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the HKMA, considers potential risks and threats arising from the Authority's day-to-day operations, including those associated with climate change. The physical impacts of climate change, such as increased flooding and other damage caused by more frequent extreme weather events, could affect the Office of the Financial Secretary's premises and impede staff commuting. To manage physical risks, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority regularly updates its Business Continuity Plan to address extreme weather events. The Monetary Authority also conducts regular evacuation and failover facility drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement continuity measures. The office design also incorporates multiple measures to mitigate potential risks. Transition risks may affect the Financial Services Authority's energy consumption, air travel, and waste management. The Monetary Authority has consistently monitored the transition risks it faces by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's climate target is to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions across Scopes 1, 2, and 3 (air travel) in all areas of its operations by 2050 or earlier. As a near-term emission reduction target, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) plans to achieve zero Scope 1 emissions by converting its entire existing vehicle fleet to electric vehicles. With 2015 as the base year, the Authority aims to reduce Scope 2 emissions intensity by 63% by 2030 or earlier through various carbon reduction and offsetting strategies. While challenges remain in determining Scope 3 emissions, the Monetary Authority will pursue a multi-pronged approach, to the extent feasible, to minimize Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, such as those from paper consumption, waste generation, and air travel. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's long-term and near-term emission reduction targets have been established in accordance with the Science Based Targets initiative methodology, which has also been validated by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has engaged the Hong Kong Productivity Council to verify the emissions, energy consumption, paper usage, and waste data disclosed in this report. The scope and criteria for verification are both detailed in the "Verification Statement" section of this report. In 2023, in addition to publishing the 2022 Annual Report, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) issued its first standalone Sustainability Report for 2022. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) enhanced work on ESG reporting has been recognized, with the HKMA receiving the ESG Award in the Public Sector category at the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "Best Corporate Governance and ESG Awards 2023." The Monetary Authority is the first financial regulator to receive an award in this category. The jury praised the HKMA for meeting robust ESG standards, noting that its Sustainability Report is clear and easy to read. The appointment of an independent body to verify its target-setting methodology and the environmental data disclosed in the report underscores the HKMA's commitment to high transparency and accountability in its reporting. In addition, the HKMA achieved the highest rating, a Gold Award, in the "Non-Profit and Charitable Organizations" category of the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants' "2023 Annual Report Awards." The panel praised the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong's annual report for its clear presentation of comprehensive financial data and its effective use of infographics, which underscore the Authority's commitment to enhancing financial literacy and promoting financial inclusion. To recognize the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) dedicated commitment to environmental stewardship, employee well-being, and the broader community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the HKMA with the "15+ Years of Shared Care" award annually for 17 consecutive years since 2006. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is committed to managing the environmental impact of its operations effectively. Its internal "Green Office Guidelines" provide staff with guidance on resource utilization and the generation of office waste. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has integrated environmental considerations into the design, operation, and maintenance of its owned and leased offices. During the office renovation, existing furniture and finishing materials will be reused to the fullest extent possible to minimize waste, and priority will be given to eco-friendly construction and decorative materials. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has consistently adopted this approach, thereby achieving LEED Gold certification for its renovated office spaces at Two International Finance Centre (IFC) in 2021, and obtaining the Green Building Council's "Green Building Council Interior Building Assessment" Gold certification in 2022. Adopting new technologies and leveraging existing technologies to enhance energy efficiency remain key priorities for the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to promoting good practices, such as turning off unnecessary lighting within office premises outside working hours to conserve electricity, other energy-saving measures include adopting LED lighting, installing motion sensors, setting air-conditioning temperatures to appropriate levels, and optimizing energy use in information technology network infrastructure. The Financial Secretary's Office's energy consumption per capita continued to decline, reaching 2.59 megawatt-hours in 2023, a 29.7% reduction from the 2015 baseline (Figure 1). Given the nature of the HKMA's daily operations, its greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions are primarily attributable to electricity consumption derived from fossil fuels. In 2023, the combined Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission intensity from purchased fuels and electricity was 1.48 tCO₂e per capita, representing a 45.2% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 2). In addition to standardizing equipment, office software, and meeting facilities, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has adopted digital tools and technologies, automated and streamlined workflows, and built a digital work environment to enhance internal collaboration through online platforms. 11. Paperless meetings have become the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's primary mode of conducting meetings. To further reduce paper consumption and enhance efficiency, all internal administrative procedures are primarily conducted through digital workflows. In addition, the HKMA encourages staff to embrace green and digital working practices by replacing paper documents and communications with digital alternatives. At the same time, work is underway to implement an electronic record-keeping system. The aforementioned green and digitalization measures have yielded positive outcomes. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) achieved a paper consumption density of 11.55 kilograms per person, representing a substantial 64.8% reduction compared to 2015 (Figure 3). Following the COVID-19 pandemic, the majority of international activities have resumed in person, and efforts to strengthen Hong Kong's position as an international financial centre have intensified. Consequently, it has become unavoidable for employees of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority to undertake official overseas assignments. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the Monetary Authority encourages employees participating in overseas activities to, where feasible, book direct flights or combine multiple business trips into a single itinerary. At the institutional level, the Monetary Authority of Singapore reduced its Scope 3 emissions by 126 tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2023 through the purchase of sustainable aviation fuel. In addition, the Monetary Authority has participated in the "Gold Standard" 12-certified carbon offset program to neutralize the remaining carbon emissions from business air travel. This program supports waste-to-energy projects, solar power generation, and the provision of efficient and cleaner cooking facilities in developing countries. The Monetary Authority will continue to implement similar arrangements in 2024. The Financial Services and Treasury Bureau's procurement process incorporates considerations for sustainable development and environmental protection. As part of a comprehensive review of the institution's procurement policies and procedures, the current practice of purchasing green products has been formalized into a standing system, in compliance with the environmental specifications of the Government's Green Procurement List, particularly for electrical appliances and office consumables. Furthermore, the tender evaluation criteria have been enhanced to incorporate ESG factors and innovative proposals aimed at improving productivity and efficiency. At the same time, all suppliers must commit to complying with environmental regulations. In accordance with the "4R" principles—Refuse, Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle—the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has adopted a three-pronged approach to minimize waste generation and effectively manage waste disposal. In addition, the HKMA conducted two waste audits in 2022 and 2023 to assist in formulating targeted waste management strategies. A detailed breakdown of the non-hazardous waste generated, including general waste sent to landfills and various categories of recyclable waste, is provided in the "Performance Summary" section on page 56. In 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) directly participated for the first time in the red envelope recycling initiative organized by the management company of the International Finance Centre. Employees turned in approximately 3,000 used red envelopes that were still in pristine condition. These red envelopes will subsequently be handed over to an environmental organization for distribution to the public for use during the upcoming Lunar New Year. Given that the operations of the Financial Services Authority (FSA) and its backup data center constitute the primary energy consumers within the institution, both data centers have been upgraded to meet the highest standards set by the Green Building Council (BEAM Plus) for existing data centers, achieving an optimal Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of 1.3. In 2023, the HKMA's two data centers were awarded "Gold" and "Platinum" ratings, respectively, under the 2021 assessment guidelines for existing data centers titled "Green Building Council's BEAM Plus Existing Data Centres." The HKMA is the first and only institution in Hong Kong to have received such ratings. Enhancing the energy efficiency of the two data centers has consistently been a key focus of the technical team. To this end, the team implemented green design principles in the renovation works and adopted energy-efficient best practices to reduce the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) and achieve relevant targets. These measures include 24-hour monitoring of data center environmental systems and continuous optimization of airflow and temperature settings. As the technical team continued to enhance energy efficiency at the data centre, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) engaged external consultants in December 2021 to conduct a comprehensive review. The review aimed to fully assess the data centre's green credentials and formulate recommendations to further improve performance across all areas. The relevant study was completed in mid-2022. Shortly after completing its study, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong also began preparations to qualify for the "Green Data Centre" certification under the "Green Building Council's BEAM Plus" certification scheme. The certification process is comprehensive and rigorous. Throughout 2023, the Technical Team implemented optimization measures in line with the consultant's recommendations to enhance energy performance and improve health-related aspects of the working environment within the data center.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency conducted independent verification of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (the "HKMA") 2023 environmental data ("2023 Data"). The 2023 data encompass total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, GHG emissions from business aviation travel, paper usage, and non-hazardous waste generated (including general waste and recyclables sent to landfills), along with their respective intensity metrics and changes relative to 2015 levels. Furthermore, the 2023 data include the amount of food waste generated during that year, its intensity, and the change compared to the baseline levels when the Monetary Authority of Singapore launched its food waste recycling programme in November 2022. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's greenhouse gas emission data have been compiled in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, a joint initiative of the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The verification scope covers data from January 1, 2023, to December 31, 2023, as well as data from January 1, 2015, to December 31, 2015, which were used for annual performance comparison (excluding food waste volumes). The verification scope covered assets across five office and warehouse locations: four offices situated at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase 1, and 4) Kowloon Trade Centre; and one warehouse located at the Luen Sang Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of the validation is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of the 2023 data and to confirm the adequacy of the data collection mechanisms of the Monetary Authority. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from five assets. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with ISAE 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB). The verification process is designed to form an opinion and draw conclusions to provide a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the selected sample data by tracing it back to its source. It also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal controls, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also included validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the 2023 data, and performing audits on a representative sample of data and information. The underlying raw data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the validation process. The Monetary Authority is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority (HKQAA) verification team did not participate in the 2023 data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance for the 2023 data and concludes that: the 2023 data are substantially accurate and reliable, and the Monetary Authority's overall data collection mechanism is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin reviewed the Hong Kong Productivity Council's April 2024 audit.

The threats posed by climate change are imminent, making accelerated global climate action urgent. The World Meteorological Organization has confirmed that 2024 was the hottest year on record and marked the first time global temperatures exceeded the critical 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels. At the same time, although global greenhouse gas emissions eased slightly during the pandemic, they have recently reached record highs, underscoring the inadequacy of current climate mitigation measures. As efforts to address global warming advance, the emergence of climate-related risks is expected to intensify, with unpredictable impacts on the economy and financial markets. Furthermore, the current geopolitical tensions, an increasingly fragmented global economic landscape, the risk of exacerbating energy security challenges, and an uncertain economic outlook collectively pose greater challenges for countries in addressing climate change. The transition to a low-carbon economy requires substantial and sustained financial support. Globally, the transition challenges are most severe, particularly in Asia. As the World Economic Forum has noted, Asia is not only the engine of global economic growth but also the region most vulnerable to the impacts of climate change. Therefore, Asia plays a pivotal role in whether the global community can successfully achieve the net-zero emissions target. As Asia's leading international financial center, Hong Kong has a responsibility to strengthen its pivotal role and fully leverage the power of finance to support and drive regional transformation. To this end, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published the Sustainable Finance Action Plan last year, setting out our vision and roadmap for progressively integrating sustainable development principles into the core of the financial system. Our work focuses on both enhancing the financial sector's capacity to manage climate-related risks and supporting the industry in capitalizing on emerging opportunities. At the same time, we lead by example and provide direction. The HKMA's sustainable development work encompasses four key areas: supporting the banking sector's transition to net-zero emissions, investing in a sustainable future, promoting net-zero financing, and advancing more inclusive sustainable development. The banking sector plays a pivotal role in the net-zero transition in Hong Kong and across Asia, yet it faces significant risks during this transformation. Under the Action Plan, we have set ambitious targets requiring all banks to achieve net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 and net-zero emissions from their financed portfolio by 2050. At the same time, we require all banks to enhance disclosures regarding climate-related risks and opportunities. While continuously strengthening banks' climate risk management, we also provide guidance for their transition planning to enhance their capacity to manage the transition and better address associated risks. We are also initiating preparatory work with relevant stakeholders to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, with the aim of further enhancing transparency across the industry in these activities. Additionally, we are refining the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification System, launched in May last year, to incorporate a broader range of sustainable activities, including transition activities. We aim to channel more capital into sustainable and transition-related projects by providing clear guidelines. Climate change poses significant physical and transition risks that may affect the long-term financial performance and value of Exchange Fund investments. At the same time, it also presents opportunities for growth and a positive impact on the Exchange Fund. Our experience demonstrates that investment returns and positive sustainability impact can be harmonized, with no inherent conflict between them. In light of this, we are committed to achieving net zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier, and have pledged in the Action Plan to support Asia's climate transition through the Fund's investments. Currently, sustainable investments account for more than 10% of the portfolio. To further promote sustainable investment in the region, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) established a strategic partnership with the Asian Development Bank, the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and the International Finance Corporation in November last year. Through co-investment, this collaboration aims to accelerate the low-carbon economic transition across Asia. Additionally, in September last year, we released our first "HKMA ESG Expectations" document to further encourage fund managers to actively exercise ownership rights and adopt sound sustainable investment practices. Financial intermediation is particularly vital for accelerating transformation within the region. As an international financial hub and the preferred venue for issuers in Asia, including provincial and municipal governments in mainland China, to arrange international sustainable bond issuances, Hong Kong plays a pivotal role in guiding capital to accelerate regional transformation. The Action Plan outlines the vision of positioning Hong Kong as the region's premier platform for sustainable finance and sets the goal of fostering innovation in sustainable finance. From leveraging the demonstration effect of the Government's Green Bond Financing Programme to spur innovation in green bonds—including the issuance in February last year of the world's first multi-currency digital bonds—to expanding the scope of the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme in May last year to cover transition financing instruments, and further to launching the Digital Bond Grant Scheme in November last year, we have remained committed to encouraging issuers within the region to utilise Hong Kong's financial platform to raise funds needed for decarbonisation and transition. To achieve a robust transition, in addition to capital and innovation, a sustainable development framework that is inclusive and accessible for participation is also required. This includes reliable sustainability data, high transparency in information disclosure, and industry professionals equipped with the requisite knowledge and skills. Accordingly, we have committed in the Action Plan to support the advancement of high-quality and comprehensive sustainability disclosure, and to address the regional shortfall in sustainability finance talent and expertise. We have made significant progress in supporting relevant stakeholders and facilitating sustainable disclosure, particularly by providing user-friendly climate disclosure templates to encourage sustainability reporting among small and medium-sized enterprises. We also launched in November last year the "Green and Sustainable Finance" Professional Level module under the Banking Professional Qualification Framework to enhance the relevant knowledge and skills of local banking professionals. In addition, through the inaugural Hong Kong Green Week held last February and other events, we have engaged stakeholders in discussions on sustainable development, thereby fostering collaboration and innovation. Within the Monetary Authority, we are committed to ensuring our operations align with our vision for sustainable development. In our Action Plan, we have committed to achieving net-zero emissions across our operations by 2030, advancing our original target by 20 years. In addition, we are proactively preparing to meet international sustainability disclosure standards in line with the roadmap issued by the government. We began adopting electric vehicles in 2024 and incorporated low-carbon emissions as a selection criterion during the procurement process. At the same time, we continue to enhance operational efficiency through digitalization, foster a culture of sustainable development within the organization, and motivate employees to actively engage in sustainability initiatives. Multilateral cooperation has long been the cornerstone of the global response to climate change; however, the restructuring of the international landscape and dramatic shifts in the geopolitical environment have introduced new variables into global climate action. However, climate change is an undeniable reality that is progressively intensifying. In addressing climate change, the current situation leaves us no room for the slightest complacency. We firmly believe that advancing an orderly and inclusive transition will help mitigate the impact of climate risks on Hong Kong's financial system while generating opportunities along the way. As we step into 2025, we will continue to forge ahead with determination, vigorously advance our sustainability initiatives, and deepen our partnerships with like-minded collaborators.
