Despite facing severe challenges, we remain steadfast in our commitment to support the construction of a sustainable future for Hong Kong, Asia, and beyond.

Climate change is a major challenge facing today's generation. As an international financial centre and a sustainability finance hub in Asia, Hong Kong is committed to playing a pioneering role in advancing sustainable development across Asia and the globe. In October 2024, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) released its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the "Action Plan"), outlining the HKMA's vision in this field, including our future direction, the timeline for achieving key objectives, and how we expect the industry to collaborate in advancing related initiatives. The HKMA plans to strengthen the capacity of Hong Kong's financial sector and the HKMA itself to address climate-related risks, and to advance the transition toward a more sustainable economy in Asia, through the formulation of strategic policies, enhanced regulatory engagement, and improved internal operations. Through active participation in international and regional discussions, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is also committed to exerting influence in shaping green and sustainable finance policies and standards at both the regional and global levels. As the banking regulator, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong focuses on enhancing the banking sector's climate resilience and supporting banks in maintaining safety and soundness as they transition toward net-zero emissions. Our key priorities for 2025 include: conducting a new round of thematic reviews on banks' climate risk management practices and holding a third round of consultation meetings to assess banks' implementation of the Monetary Authority's regulatory requirements and further strengthen their climate risk management capabilities; enhancing the integration of climate risk stress testing into the Monetary Authority's regulator-led stress testing framework; continuing to advance the incorporation of climate factors into the Monetary Authority's supervisory review processes; preparing regulatory guidelines for local banks to implement the upcoming Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision and the International Sustainability Reporting Standards (ISSB Standards); finalizing the development of a new chapter, GS-2, in the Supervisory Policy Manual to provide guidance on transition planning for banks; and sharing best practices with the industry on climate risk management and the application of green financial technology. Beyond its role as the banking regulator, the Monetary Authority also serves as a facilitator, committed to fostering the development of a green and sustainable finance ecosystem and supporting banks in providing financing for the transition. We have launched Phase I of the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Taxonomy to equip the industry with a tool for identifying green and sustainable economic activities and to facilitate related capital flows. The Monetary Authority has launched the second phase of the taxonomy work to broaden its scope, incorporating transition elements, expanding the range of green economic activities, and integrating adaptation objectives related to climate change. Furthermore, building on the success of the 2024 third FiNETech event and the 2023 Green Fintech Competition, we will host another Green Fintech event in 2025 to encourage banks to adopt green fintech solutions. Hong Kong possesses advantageous conditions that support the region's sustainable financing needs. To strengthen this role, we will continue to support the government in implementing the Government Sustainability Bond Scheme, whose expanded scope will now include sustainability projects such as social responsibility initiatives. This move will help deepen the development of the local green and sustainable bond market and set an example for other potential issuers in the region. Furthermore, we will continue to provide funding through the Green and Sustainable Finance Grant Scheme to encourage more borrowers in the region to leverage Hong Kong's financing platforms to raise sustainable capital. We will also enhance our promotional efforts to encourage more government bodies, organizations, and enterprises from Mainland China and other regions to raise green funds in Hong Kong. At the same time, we will continue to catalyze and support sustainable financial innovation, including providing funding to prospective issuers of digital green bonds through the Digital Bond Grant Scheme. While there is growing market demand for high-quality sustainability disclosures from institutions and enterprises, the capacity and readiness of different entities to make such disclosures vary, and some may require additional guidance and support. In light of this, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to collaborate with other members of the Cross-Sectoral Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance to make sustainable disclosure more accessible and inclusive. For instance, we will continue to provide banks and their clients with a richer suite of climate disclosure tools, including user-friendly sustainability disclosure templates and supporting resources; explore how technology can further enhance the accessibility and usability of existing resources; and collaborate with key local industry associations to deliver training tailored to industry needs. The sustainable finance market is dynamic and ever-evolving, necessitating the expansion of the local talent pool and the filling of knowledge gaps in Hong Kong and the broader region. In 2025, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's key priorities include collaborating with the banking sector to develop professional-level training courses under the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit of the Banking Professional Qualifications Framework, and identifying areas where the industry requires further training through the upcoming "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030" study. Furthermore, we plan to collaborate with key stakeholders to enhance the promotion of the government-funded "Pilot Programme on Green and Sustainable Finance Training" and to review the programme's scope of applicability. At the regional level, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will continue to collaborate with the International Finance Corporation through the Green Banking Alliance to launch a dedicated initiative in Asia. This initiative will include conducting green finance research, providing unique market analysis, offering targeted skills enhancement and training support, fostering community engagement, facilitating potential green investment opportunities, and delivering practical guidance to assist banks in developing roadmaps to integrate green finance as a core business function. As a responsible investor, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) is committed to achieving net-zero emissions for the Exchange Fund's investment portfolio by 2050 or earlier, in support of the broader economic transition. We will continuously enhance the sustainability of Exchange Fund investments through a pragmatic and rigorous responsible investment approach, focusing primarily on the long-term resilience of the portfolio while exploring investment opportunities that deliver positive climate outcomes. The Monetary Authority is committed to setting an example for organizations in advancing sustainable development. In response to the accelerated timeline to net-zero commitments announced in the Action Plan, the HKMA will pragmatically and progressively integrate environmental and social factors into its strategy, risk assessment, and reporting, continuing to advance sustainable development across the financial sector. Specifically, in 2025, we will conduct a double materiality assessment to deepen our understanding of the potential financial and non-financial impacts of climate change and other sustainability issues, ensuring our focus remains on material topics. In addition, we will conduct energy audits and leverage technological solutions to assess the material impacts of climate risks on our offices and operations, thereby enhancing our climate resilience and risk preparedness. We support the Hong Kong Government's "Hong Kong Sustainability Disclosure Roadmap" and are actively preparing to make disclosures in accordance with the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB). In 2025, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong will continue to uphold its commitment to select data centers for planned upgrade projects in accordance with energy efficiency and energy conservation principles. We will also expand our digital initiatives to advance sustainability and enhance efficiency. This includes developing digital tools and platforms to support paperless processes and waste reduction, while elevating the overall digital experience for our employees, our bank, and the public.

Climate change impacts every aspect of human life, and everyone can contribute to mitigating its effects. Through its multifaceted roles as central bank, banking regulator, market enabler, responsible investor, and sustainability institution, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong contributes to advancing and accelerating Hong Kong's, and indeed the entire Asia-Pacific region's, transition to net-zero emissions. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has established a robust sustainable governance framework to lead the formulation of relevant strategies and policies, oversee the implementation of related measures, and ensure that MAS's own operations and working methods integrate sustainability considerations. To uphold sound corporate governance, the HKMA has established a robust sustainability governance framework characterized by clear accountability arrangements and high transparency. The governance framework ensures that the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's strategic planning and decision-making processes effectively incorporate sustainability factors, and establishes robust mechanisms to monitor and evaluate the progress and outcomes of sustainability initiatives. The HKMA's sustainable development governance framework comprises: the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee (EFAC) and its related sub-committees, which oversee the HKMA's work, including its efforts in sustainable development, and provide recommendations; the Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (Steering Committee), chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, responsible for leading the HKMA's overall environmental, social, and governance (ESG) strategy and policy at the management level; within the realm of responsible investment, the ESG Committee under the Exchange Fund Investment Office coordinates and oversees ESG-related activities within that office; and for other functional areas, relevant working groups and task forces are responsible for planning and implementing sustainable development measures covering banking and market development, as well as the HKMA's own operations. At the cross-sector level, the Green and Sustainable Finance Cross-Industry Coordination Group (the Coordination Group), jointly established by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), is responsible for coordinating the efforts of financial regulators, government departments, industry stakeholders, and other relevant parties to accelerate the development of green and sustainable finance in Hong Kong. In view of the significant expansion of the scope of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) sustainable development initiatives over the past several years, we established a Steering Committee in October 2023 as a central platform to lead and more effectively coordinate all sustainable development activities across the HKMA's various functional areas. - Provide guidance on the formulation of strategies, policies, and plans concerning ESG matters across four functional areas: the banking sector, the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, Exchange Fund investments, and internal operations;  - Oversee the implementation of ESG-related initiatives by the HKMA's various functional departments;  - Assess the HKMA's performance and effectiveness in achieving its ESG objectives; and  - Supervise external communication strategies. The Supervisory Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA), with its three Deputy Chief Executives serving as ex officio members. Additionally, we will invite Assistant Executive Vice Presidents from key functions related to green and sustainable development to attend Steering Committee meetings to report on their key achievements and future plans. The Supervisory Committee convenes regular meetings, supported by relevant working groups under the Banking Division, Institutional Development and Operations Department, External Affairs Department, and the Exchange Fund Investment Office of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. In addition to formulating and implementing their own sustainable development initiatives, the HKMA and the SFC jointly established a Steering Committee in May 2020. The Steering Committee, as a cross-agency platform, provides strategic direction and coordinates cross-sector efforts within the financial industry to address climate and environmental risks, thereby strengthening Hong Kong's position as a leading green and sustainable finance hub in Asia and globally. For detailed information on the Working Group's activities, please refer to the chapter titled "Strengthening the Ecosystem for Green and Sustainable Finance."

Climate change can pose risks to the financial system. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority has consistently worked to strengthen the Hong Kong financial system's capacity to address climate risks, while contributing to Hong Kong's climate goals and the global sustainable development agenda. Banks face a range of sustainability and climate-related impacts in their daily operations and must therefore proactively manage climate risks. At the same time, banks play a pivotal role in the financial system by directing capital toward green and sustainable projects. As the banking regulator, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has focused on strengthening banks' capacity to address and manage climate-related risks, while accelerating their efforts to support the transition to a low-carbon economic model. In October, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) announced its "Sustainable Finance Action Plan," outlining its vision to further consolidate Hong Kong's position as a regional sustainable finance hub and support sustainable development across Asia and the globe. The Action Plan encompasses eight goals across four key areas. To assist the industry in achieving the objectives of the relevant banking policies, we have been carrying out the following initiatives. All banks are committed to achieving net-zero emissions from their own operations by 2030 or earlier, and net-zero emissions from their financed portfolio by 2050 or earlier. All banks will enhance transparency on climate-related risks and opportunities. In December, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) shared good practices on transition planning with the industry and launched a public consultation on the draft of Unit GS-2 "Transition Planning" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The new module aims to provide guidance on enhancing banks' capacity to manage the net-zero transition and the associated risks. In addition, we are reviewing the regulatory examination procedures used to assess and monitor banks' capital adequacy levels and to determine their Pillar 2 capital requirements. The objective is to incorporate factors identified by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision (BCBS) regarding the effective management of climate-related financial risks into the assessment process, and to encourage banks to strengthen their risk management frameworks—including transition planning—to address climate risks. The HKMA has consistently worked to align Hong Kong's sustainability disclosure requirements with international standards, including the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) standards and the Basel Committee's Pillar 3 disclosure framework on climate-related financial risks. Specifically, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) is analysing the latest developments in sustainable disclosure and supporting the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants (HKICPA) in conducting a technical feasibility study on the adoption of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards issued by the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB). Promoting green and transition finance is key to implementing the Action Plan. In May, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) published the Hong Kong Sustainable Finance Classification Scheme to address industry concerns about greenwashing and to help channel capital toward green and sustainable activities. The classification framework covers 12 economic activities across four sectors, designed to align with the Common Taxonomy as well as the classification systems of mainland China and the European Union, while also incorporating elements tailored to local conditions. We have launched the second phase of our work to expand the scope of the classification taxonomy and are actively consulting a broad range of stakeholders to further facilitate the flow of green and sustainable finance. Throughout the year, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority further strengthened its supervision of banks' climate risk management and remained committed to supporting banks in building their capacity to manage climate-related risks and opportunities and to respond to climate change. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has completed all work required under its two-year plan, established in 2022, to integrate climate risk into the banking regulatory framework. To enhance banks' capacity to manage climate-related risks, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) has shared best practices observed during thematic reviews and consultation meetings with the banking sector. These practices primarily include: establishing a robust governance framework that clearly defines the responsibilities of the board of directors and senior management; and ensuring effective oversight of key areas of climate-related risks, namely: (1) promoting and monitoring the effective formulation and implementation of climate strategies; (2) implementing appropriate oversight of climate-related risk management; and (3) fostering a sound climate risk culture within institutions. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority hosted a balanced regulation roundtable in August focused on climate risk management. At the roundtable meeting, representatives of banks and participants from the Monetary Authority exchanged views on several climate risk-related topics, including the challenges banks face in climate risk management, climate risk stress testing, transition planning, and finance. This roundtable provided an interactive platform for information sharing and will assist the Hong Kong Monetary Authority in its work on climate risk regulation and other related areas. The HKMA launched a thematic review of banks' climate risk management frameworks and practices, assessing their robustness and adequacy in line with the supervisory expectations set out in GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual. The thematic review covers the entire risk management process, including risk identification, measurement, monitoring, reporting, control, and mitigation, as well as climate risk scenario analysis and stress testing. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority convened its second round of consultation meetings to assess the progress of a new batch of banks in implementing Unit GS-1 "Climate Risk Management" of the Supervisory Policy Manual and to understand the challenges they face. The consultation meeting also covered the latest regulatory and market developments in climate-related fields, including transition planning, disclosure frameworks and standards, as well as issues of greenwashing. We provide feedback and guidance tailored to each bank's specific circumstances to support their climate risk management efforts. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) completed the second round of the Climate Risk Stress Test (CRST) for the banking sector in 2024, with participation from 21 retail banks and the Hong Kong branches of 25 international banking groups. The results indicate that, across a range of scenarios—including those assuming simultaneous climate risks and a downturn in the macroeconomic environment—the Hong Kong banking sector continues to demonstrate robust resilience against severe climate-related shocks. Compared with the CRST pilot program, participating banks have significantly enhanced their capabilities in measuring and assessing climate-related risks. A report outlining the results of the CRST and the good practices observed by the Monetary Authority during the process was published in February 2025. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) recognizes that banks face numerous challenges regarding data and methodologies in climate risk management. Accordingly, it has been actively pursuing multiple initiatives to promote the application of technology in addressing these challenges. To address the lack of physical risk data and analytical tools for climate risk assessment, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched a Physical Risk Assessment Platform in May, enabling banks to evaluate the potential impacts of physical risks on Hong Kong's residential and commercial buildings under various climate scenarios. Looking ahead, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority will enhance the platform by incorporating user feedback and additional local data. In addition, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has collaborated with relevant stakeholders to promote the adoption of green fintech solutions by banks and the broader financial services sector. This year, we have released practical application guidelines and two English-language "RegTech Use Case Briefs" that outline technology solutions for environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and sustainability assessments, as well as for greenwashing risk management. We also hosted the third "FiNETech" forum, bringing together over 150 financial institutions and technology companies to explore collaborations in green fintech. The Monetary Authority recognizes that climate change may pose potential risks to the financial system; accordingly, it has expanded the scope of climate-related factors and scenarios incorporated into financial risk analysis and research to strengthen current monitoring efforts. In its ongoing monitoring of financial stability risks, the Monetary Authority will take climate change into account and incorporate analyses of climate-related risks into its various financial stability reports. By actively participating in the Scenario Design and Analysis Working Group under the Network for Greening the Financial System (NGFS), the HKMA has helped further enrich climate scenarios, thereby assisting central banks and regulators in understanding the impacts of climate change on the macroeconomy and the financial system. In November, the NGFS released its fifth edition of long-term climate macro-financial scenarios, providing a reference for forward-looking climate risk assessment. As a member of the Transition Planning Task Force under the Financial Stability Board, the HKMA has contributed to analyzing the interplay between transition planning by financial and non-financial companies and financial stability, enabling policymakers to assess climate-related financial risks through a forward-looking and dynamic lens. The Monetary Authority of Singapore has issued the "Practical Guide on Banks' Adoption of Green Technology" (English version), offering financial institutions best practices for leveraging green technologies to advance their net-zero transition. In terms of research, the HKMA has undertaken several applied research projects to examine the impact of climate change on the financial sector and the broader economy. Research topics include the cross-border transmission of climate transition risks, the role of corporate environmental performance in shielding against monetary policy shocks, the impact of climate-related factors on the flow of foreign direct investment, and the financial sector's role in the transition to a low-carbon economy. The aforementioned research findings not only deepen our understanding of how climate change affects financial stability but also offer valuable insights into the green and sustainable finance ecosystem, thereby informing the development of relevant policies. Locally, these studies will strengthen the HKMA's ongoing monitoring and assessment of the impact of climate change on financial stability. Research findings are also shared with a broad spectrum of stakeholders through various channels, including international forums and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Research Memoranda. The Hong Kong Monetary and Financial Research Centre, the research unit under the Faculty of Business Administration, has published a research paper examining the impact of carbon pricing on corporate performance. The study provides evidence that low-emission enterprises can derive significant benefits from carbon pricing, highlighting its role in enhancing efficiency by reallocating resources from high-emission to low-emission enterprises. The study, published in the Research Centre's "Insights from Monetary Research," has been shared with local and international scholars and policy researchers. The HKMA's Liquidity Facility Framework is a secured standby funding arrangement that provides timely liquidity support to banks in need. The HKMA has incorporated sustainability considerations into its assessment of eligible collateral under this framework. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is actively engaged in international and regional discussions on addressing climate risks and advancing sustainable finance as a mainstream priority. Through such engagement, we contribute to advancing policy dialogue on addressing climate change and its implications for financial stability at both the international and regional levels, while drawing on these insights to strengthen Hong Kong's financial system's climate resilience.

To consolidate Hong Kong's position as the region's leading hub for green and sustainable finance, the HKMA is committed to enhancing market awareness and participation, providing the necessary infrastructure and catalysts, and supporting relevant international initiatives to align with global standards. As outlined in the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) "Sustainable Finance Action Plan" (the Action Plan), the HKMA is committed to enhancing the green and sustainable finance ecosystem by advancing net-zero financing and fostering more inclusive sustainable development. Specifically, we are committed to positioning Hong Kong as the leading platform for sustainable financing for borrowers, both regionally and globally; fostering technological innovation in the green segment of financial markets; enhancing sustainability disclosure across the industry; expanding the local pool of green talent; and addressing knowledge gaps in sustainable finance in Hong Kong and the region. To position Hong Kong as the premier platform for sustainable financing in the region and globally, catalyzing sustainable finance innovation, supporting high-quality and comprehensive sustainable disclosure, and addressing the regional shortfall in sustainable finance talent and expertise, the Government launched the Government Green Bond Program in 2018. This initiative demonstrates the Government's resolve to address climate change, advance green finance, and foster Hong Kong's development into a more sustainable and liveable city. To date, the Monetary Authority has assisted the Government in issuing approximately USD 28 billion worth of green bonds to institutional and retail investors. The funds raised have been allocated to more than 110 government green projects, including green building, waste management and recycling, energy efficiency, and energy conservation. We seize every issuance opportunity to continuously innovate and expand the features of green bonds, including currencies, tenors, and distribution channels, thereby laying a foundation for other public and private green bond issuers in the region. In 2024, to enhance the plan's impact and further solidify Hong Kong's position as a hub for green and sustainable finance, the plan's scope was expanded to include sustainable projects and it was renamed the "Government Sustainable Bond Scheme" (the Sustainable Bond Scheme). To enhance the transparency and accountability of the Green Bond Framework, the Government publishes an annual Green Bond Report, detailing the allocation of proceeds raised from green bonds and their anticipated environmental benefits. In July, the Monetary Authority of Singapore assisted the government in issuing approximately USD 3 billion worth of institutional green bonds under the Sustainable Bonds Framework. This tri-currency issuance includes bonds in various maturities denominated in Renminbi, US dollars, and euros. The bond issuance attracted participation from a diverse range of investors, generating a robust subscription response with total subscriptions exceeding $15 billion in equivalent value. The 20- and 30-year RMB green bonds represent the government's first issuance of such instruments, marking the longest tenor RMB bonds issued to date. They establish a new benchmark for the market and further enhance the demonstrative role of the Sustainable Bond Initiative. These bonds further broaden the range of offshore renminbi investment products available in Hong Kong. Furthermore, the strong response from global investors to government-issued green bonds reflects their endorsement of Hong Kong's commitment to advancing green and sustainable development. To encourage more borrowers within the region to tap into Hong Kong's financing platform for raising sustainable development funds, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) continues to implement the Green and Sustainable Finance Subsidy Scheme, launched in May 2021, which provides subsidies for eligible green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong. The initiative has garnered widespread acclaim within the industry. As of the end of 2024, it has provided funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a combined total exceeding USD 140 billion. The plan was extended for three years until 2027 in May 2024 and expanded to include financing for transition bonds and loans. The purpose of extending and expanding the scheme is to encourage relevant industry borrowers in the region to leverage Hong Kong's transition finance platform to gradually reduce their carbon emissions. - Provided funding for approximately 500 green and sustainable debt instruments issued in Hong Kong, with a total issuance value exceeding USD 140 billion (as of end-2024). The funding scheme has been extended by three years to 2027 and expanded to cover transition finance instruments. Meanwhile, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has actively promoted Hong Kong's sustainable finance platform, achieving satisfactory results. In August, the Shenzhen Municipal People's Government issued its fourth offshore local government bond in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 7 billion, comprising RMB 2.7 billion in green bonds, RMB 1 billion in sustainability bonds, and RMB 900 million in social responsibility bonds. In September, the Guangdong Provincial Government issued offshore bonds for the first time in Hong Kong, totaling RMB 5 billion, including RMB 1.5 billion in green bonds. In October, the Hainan Provincial Government also issued offshore bonds in Hong Kong for the third time, with a total value of RMB 3 billion, comprising RMB 1 billion in blue bonds and RMB 1 billion in sustainable bonds. These bond issuance activities repeatedly underscore Hong Kong's unique role in facilitating green and sustainable capital flows between the Mainland and the rest of the world. Through the implementation of these measures, Hong Kong has strengthened its position as the preferred platform for sustainable finance in Asia. According to statistics released by the International Capital Market Association (ICMA), Hong Kong remained Asia's leading hub for the issuance of international green and sustainable bonds in 2024, with a total of $43.1 billion in such bonds arranged through the city, accounting for 45% of the regional total. To catalyze innovation in sustainable finance, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) assisted the government in issuing two landmark tokenized green bonds in 2023 and 2024: the world's first tokenized sovereign green bonds and the world's first multi-currency digital bonds. The issuance underscores the government's support for market participants in the region to leverage asset digitization and innovative technologies in the fields of green and sustainable finance. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority also launched the Digital Bond Funding Scheme in November to promote the issuance of digital bonds in Hong Kong, including digital green bonds, thereby encouraging and supporting innovation and development in the city's green and sustainable finance markets. The Working Group on Sustainable Disclosure, established under the Cross-Industry Steering Group on Green and Sustainable Finance (the Steering Group), has been actively working towards the adoption of the International Financial Reporting Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) in Hong Kong. In December 2024, the Government issued the "Hong Kong Sustainable Disclosure Roadmap," which sets out a clear pathway for large public-interest entities to fully adopt the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards (ISSB Standards) no later than 2028. The HKMA has maintained close collaboration with local and international partners to support entities at various stages of preparation in achieving high-quality sustainable disclosures, thereby making sustainable disclosures more accessible and inclusive. Notably, we continue to encourage the application of the "Climate and Environmental Risk Questionnaire for Unlisted Companies" (the Questionnaire), which the Supervisory Group launched in collaboration with CDP in 2022. The questionnaire provides user-friendly disclosure templates to facilitate sustainability reporting for businesses, including small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The questionnaire was launched in its electronic format in February 2024 to facilitate online submission by enterprises (see the QR code below). The Monetary Authority is refining the survey questionnaire based on industry feedback and the latest international developments to enhance its usability. Specific measures include identifying core questions within the survey and providing common usage scenarios for the questionnaire. Furthermore, we also strive to enhance the compatibility of the questionnaire and other supporting tools on the Supervisory Committee's website. For more information on the questionnaire, please refer to the relevant webpage. In line with its commitment, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has proactively adopted the latest global standards to deliver high-quality sustainability disclosures in its Sustainability Report. The report contains rich content on the HKMA's climate-related institutional operational risks, as well as plans and progress in implementing measures to achieve climate goals. For detailed disclosures regarding the sustainability of our own operations, please refer to the chapter titled "The Sustainable HKMA." Given the dynamic nature of the sustainable finance market, the HKMA is enhancing skills training for the banking sector and fostering knowledge sharing with other regulators and international stakeholders to address gaps in expertise and talent. To enhance the knowledge and skills of local banking professionals in sustainable finance, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) collaborated with The Hong Kong Institute of Bankers (HKIB) to launch the Foundation Level of the "Green and Sustainable Finance" unit under the Banking Competency Framework in July 2023. This unit is designed to enable banking professionals to acquire knowledge in green and sustainable finance more effectively and to develop relevant professional competencies. It covers four key areas: (1) green and sustainable finance products and services; (2) sustainable and climate risk management; (3) sustainability disclosure and reporting; and (4) sustainable strategy, compliance, and governance. In addition, the professional-level module on "Green and Sustainable Finance" for senior and middle-level banking professionals responsible for related work was launched in November. To provide necessary training for banking professionals, the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers, as the managing body for the "Green and Sustainable Finance" module, launched the introductory-level training course for this module in May. Following the launch of the professional level in November, the HKMA will, in collaboration with the banking sector in 2025, develop professional-level training curricula. To better understand the evolving skills and training needs of the banking sector, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is currently collaborating with the banking industry on a study titled "Future Banking Talent 2026–2030," with the aim of publishing its findings in 2025. This joint study follows the publication of the document "Future Banking Talent 2021–2025" in June 2020. The findings of this follow-up study will serve as a critical reference for the industry, aiding in the formulation and adjustment of talent development strategies and measures to support the sustainable development of the banking sector. The Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAH) continues to support the implementation of the government-funded "Pilot Scheme for Green and Sustainable Finance Training" in collaboration with the Steering Committee, providing funding for industry practitioners, graduates, and students to undertake training in sustainable finance. As of December 2024, the scheme had registered 85 international and local courses as eligible training programs and had approved over 5,700 reimbursement applications. The Government announced in the 2025-26 Budget that the scheme will be extended until 2028. The Monetary Authority is committed to leveraging its expertise, through regional and international cooperation, to promote skills training and knowledge sharing. As a founding member of the Coalition for Sustainable Investment Capacity Building (CASI), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's Infrastructure Financing Promotion Office co-hosted a two-day training workshop with CASI in Hong Kong in June, focusing on the global sustainable finance market, policy frameworks, and innovative tools. Furthermore, the HKMA supports the establishment of the Glasgow Financial Alliance for Net Zero (GFANZ) Hong Kong office in October and will leverage GFANZ's network and expertise to enhance capacity-building in transition planning and transition finance.

As a significant global owner and manager of assets, the Monetary Authority actively leads the development of green and sustainable finance. Drawing on its experience in demonstrating that strong financial performance and positive impact can reinforce one another, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong upholds a responsible investment approach in managing the Exchange Fund, prioritizing sustainable assets and requiring its external investment managers to actively exercise stewardship. The Monetary Authority invests prudently on the principle of "capital preservation first, long-term growth thereafter," and believes that fully incorporating environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors can help mitigate investment risks while unlocking the long-term sustainable value of investments. As a steadfast signatory of the Principles for Responsible Investment (PRI), the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is committed to advancing its responsible investment initiatives. We place particular emphasis on sustainability, especially the urgent challenge of climate change, with the aim of enhancing the resilience of the Exchange Fund and securing improved risk-adjusted long-term returns. We integrate ESG factors in a pragmatic and orderly manner, continuously exploring a range of investment tools to channel capital into sustainable investments across diverse asset classes (Figure 1). Leveraging its role as a major investor, the Monetary Authority contributes to the advancement of the green and sustainable finance ecosystem. In September, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) released the "HKMA ESG Expectations" and made the document available to its investment partners through annual ESG workshops and the HKMA website. We collaborate with investors, regulatory bodies, and international organizations that share our vision to develop industry operating standards and promote the adoption of responsible investment practices across the financial sector and central banking community. Through these collaborative efforts, we are committed to fostering a future where finance and sustainable development advance hand in hand. In October, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong released its Sustainable Finance Action Plan, outlining its commitment to achieve net-zero emissions by 2050 or earlier through the Investment Portfolio of the Exchange Fund, mobilizing partners to support the transition to a low-carbon economy, and further solidifying its dedication to investing in a sustainable future. The Exchange Fund Advisory Committee, chaired by the Financial Secretary, has established a framework and guiding principles for responsible investment, which are implemented by the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund in the management of the Exchange Fund's investments. The primary guiding principles establish the tone for the Exchange Fund to pursue responsible investment while simultaneously meeting the investment objectives of the Fund. The Investment Committee under the Exchange Fund Advisory Committee is chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority and is responsible for overseeing ESG and climate-related risks associated with Exchange Fund investment projects. The Investment Committee reviews the Responsible Investment Framework and risk management policies and monitors their implementation through regular reporting by the Sustainable Investment Group of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. As illustrated in Figure 2, the ESG Committee under the Investment Office of the Exchange Fund is chaired by the Chief Strategy Officer and is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the Investment Office's ESG initiatives. The motions and progress updates discussed by the ESG Committee at its quarterly meetings will be reported to the Chief Executive of the Exchange Fund Investment Office. In addition, the Green and Sustainable Oversight Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAHK) and with the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Strategy Officer of the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) as members, convenes regular meetings to provide guidance on ESG policies and initiatives across various MAHK functions, including the EFIO, thereby advancing the MAHK's overall ESG objectives. The Sustainable Investment Group collaborates closely with separate teams within the Exchange Fund Investment Office (EFIO) to integrate ESG factors and assists EFIO senior management in overseeing ESG, particularly climate-related, risks and opportunities across various investment portfolios:  - Public Market Investments: The Credit, Regulation and Oversight Committee, composed of EFIO senior executives, reviews how ESG factors are incorporated into credit risk models based on the Sustainable Investment Group's recommendations. Additionally, the ESG status of fixed-income portfolios is monitored through regular reporting from the Risk Management and Oversight Department. In addition, the Sustainable Investment Group participates in the selection, appointment, and oversight of external investment managers for the equity portfolio from an ESG perspective (see the section "Promoting Active Ownership" under "Risk Management" on page 39 for further details). - Private market investment: The Investment Committee, chaired by the Chief Executive Officer of the Monetary Authority, will review private market investment proposals alongside the ESG-related assessments conducted by the Risk Management team for each proposal. The Exchange Fund understands that the physical and transition risks posed by climate change, as well as the associated opportunities, will affect the long-term financial performance of its investment portfolio. The United Nations Environment Programme's 2024 Emissions Gap Report projects that, without a global-scale mobilization to rapidly cut greenhouse gas emissions, global average temperatures will rise by 2.6 to 3.1 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels. Policy responses to the uncertainties surrounding rising temperatures, technological advancements, and behavioral shifts may exacerbate transition risks, leading to increased market volatility and affecting asset valuations. At the same time, the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather events are exposing investment projects to additional risks of physical damage and financial losses. Amid these challenges, governments and industries are turning to sustainable solutions, thereby creating potentially attractive long-term investment opportunities in low-carbon solutions, emerging technologies, and sustainable infrastructure. The Exchange Fund believes that investing in a sustainable future aligns with its investment objectives; accordingly, it places particular emphasis on climate-related factors when integrating ESG considerations. The Exchange Fund has set a target for its investment portfolio to reach net zero emissions by 2050 or earlier, and is advancing this goal through an orderly, three-pronged approach (see Figure 3). In 2024, the Monetary Authority announced an Action Plan that reinforced the Exchange Fund's commitments and efforts related to climate transition (see Figure 4). To support the transition to a low-carbon economy, the Monetary Authority prefers proactive engagement over divestment or exclusion from investable projects. Investing in a Sustainable Future Foreign Exchange Fund Portfolio: Achieve net-zero emissions by 2050; actively expand the scope and variety of sustainable investments, particularly climate-transition-themed investments in both public and private markets; integrate ESG factors into every investment decision, with a particular focus on climate change and transition prospects; establish clear, internationally aligned ESG expectations based on best practices, and require all external investment managers, investee companies, and counterparties to adhere to them; commit to reducing the weighted average carbon intensity (WACI) of the Foreign Exchange Fund's equity portfolio by 67% from 2017 levels by 2030; support regional transformation through investment; continue engaging with external investment managers to optimize opportunities that drive transition; and continue identifying and prioritizing high-quality investment opportunities that advance Asia's transformation and generate positive global impacts. First, maintaining a diversified and robust asset portfolio is crucial to achieving the Foreign Exchange Fund's primary investment objective. Excluding certain sectors or industries outright would narrow the investable universe and could potentially impact investment returns and risk. Through a phased approach, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority is able to seize opportunities to invest in companies undergoing transformation that demonstrate strong technological capabilities and sound corporate governance to address evolving global climate trends, including those in high-emission sectors. Second, addressing climate change requires the transformation of core "brown" industries. Merely excluding relevant investment projects or divesting is insufficient to address carbon emission challenges. In contrast, the Monetary Authority has supported these sectors by deploying strategic capital and actively exercising ownership rights, thereby driving their transition to sustainable and low-carbon operational practices. This approach has generated positive outcomes not only for the Authority itself but also for the global community. The Net Zero investment strategy has evolved from favoring green or low-carbon assets to encompassing assets with credible transition prospects, thereby driving comprehensive decarbonization across the entire economy. As a global asset owner, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority recognizes that the long-term resilience of an investment portfolio depends not only on internal portfolio adjustments but also on broader economic transformation. While no single perfect solution exists, in 2024 the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong enhanced its responsible investment strategy by adopting a comprehensive and diversified approach to advance the transition, while supporting the Exchange Fund and the global net-zero objective. This strategy integrates top-down and bottom-up tools, including the incorporation of ESG factors into fundamental analysis, portfolio decarbonization tilts, and thematic investments in asset classes aligned with pathways to net-zero emissions. In the public markets, this may involve tilting the portfolio toward ESG leaders or providers of climate solutions, while supporting supervisory efforts to drive corporate transformation. In the private equity market, there may be a greater emphasis on investment projects that promote transformation. By integrating ESG factors into investment decisions, the Monetary Authority continues to seek investment opportunities that advance climate transition while enhancing the long-term resilience of the Exchange Fund's portfolio. Sustainable investments across different asset classes account for more than 10% of the Exchange Fund's portfolio, with financial performance broadly in line with that of the corresponding asset class benchmarks (Figure 5). - Public market investments – The Exchange Fund launched an active global equity portfolio focused on sustainability and climate transition, and expanded the application of a customized low-carbon stock index to two additional portfolios managed by external investment managers. The Monetary Authority continues to pursue the issuance of competitive green, social, and sustainability (GSS) bonds that provide funding for sustainable projects while delivering attractive returns (see the case study "Enhancing Sustainability through GSS Bonds"). - Private market investment – The Monetary Authority is committed to building a resilient long-term growth portfolio, capitalizing on investment opportunities aligned with climate and energy transition themes. Leveraging its extensive network and expertise, the Monetary Authority has actively identified and evaluated investment opportunities to accelerate the energy transition, including by forging strategic partnerships with multinational organizations (see the section "Working Together to Address Climate Challenges Across Asia and Beyond"). - Passive portfolios benchmarked to ESG indices - Customized decarbonization strategies for passive and active quantitative portfolios with non-ESG benchmarks - Active portfolios focused on governance - Active ESG portfolios centered on sustainability and climate transition - Sustainable-themed projects, such as renewable energy infrastructure and green-certified buildings and warehouses - Funds focused on energy transition and decarbonization in global, Asian, and Global South contexts - Green, social, and sustainability bonds - A green bond fund managed by an international organization - The "Multilateral Credit Portfolio Management Program" (MCPP), managed by the International Finance Corporation, with a focus on sustainable investments in emerging markets - The "MCPP One Planet" initiative, which provides climate-related investment funding for emerging markets aligned with the Paris Agreement. The regulator invests in green bonds issued by a semi-official institution. The proceeds from the green bond have been allocated to multiple projects, including the upgrading of aging equipment at several wastewater treatment facilities. These upgrade projects encompass the optimization of monitoring and control systems, as well as pump performance, to generate positive environmental benefits through wastewater management, waste reduction, and recycling processes. In addition to continuing to treat wastewater and sludge, these facilities will compost or reuse dewatered sludge to produce fertilizers, charcoal, cement, and other construction materials, achieving a sludge recovery rate of up to 100%. These facilities also utilize gas generated during the sludge treatment process to provide energy for boilers and generate electricity. The Monetary Authority invested in a green bond issued by a multilateral development bank. The bond will provide financing for multiple projects, including the restoration of a national canal system. As one of the country's largest irrigation systems, the canal is designed to divert excess river water to arid regions. The primary objective of this project is to repair the increasingly deteriorating canal lining to prevent seepage, conserve water, improve water-use efficiency, and reclaim waterlogged areas. In addition, the project has provided skills training for local stakeholders and promoted the adoption and effective use of modern irrigation technologies, such as micro-irrigation, alongside sustainable farming practices.

The Monetary Authority is committed to being a responsible and sustainable institution. In 2024, one of the key priorities of the Monetary Authority of Singapore in fulfilling this commitment was to advance the target for achieving net-zero emissions in institutional operations to 2030, 20 years ahead of the original timeline, in line with the Sustainable Finance Action Plan. In addition to advancing environmental sustainability, the Monetary Authority has pledged to foster employee training and well-being, promote financial inclusion, and enhance the public's financial literacy. The Green and Sustainable Development Steering Committee (the Steering Committee), chaired by the Chief Executive of the Monetary Authority, serves as the primary decision-making body for all institutional sustainable development initiatives. To demonstrate the HKMA's commitment to addressing climate change, the Supervisory Committee approved in October 2024 a new target for the HKMA to achieve net-zero emissions from its own operations by 2030 or earlier, as part of the Sustainable Finance Action Plan ("the Action Plan"). At the departmental level, the Assistant President (Institutional Development and Operations) provides guidance on implementing sustainable development measures in institutional operations, employee well-being, and community engagement, and submits regular reports to the Steering Committee. The Administrative Section serves as the coordinator and central hub for implementing, disseminating, and reporting on sustainable development initiatives. Green Office task forces and volunteer service groups, composed of staff from various operational departments, provide an additional layer of support. The former serves as a platform for brainstorming and proposing initiatives to foster a green workplace, while the latter aims to cultivate a culture of employee engagement in volunteer activities. To recognize the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) sustained commitment to environmental stewardship, employee well-being, and the broader community, the Hong Kong Council of Social Service has presented the "15+ Years of Caring Together" mark to the HKMA for 18 consecutive years, from 2006 to 2024. The HKMA's sustainable development strategy continues to be structured around three core pillars: the environment, employees, and social responsibility. - Focus on the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) daily operations by advancing decarbonization and digitalization, with the goal of achieving net-zero emissions by 2030 or earlier.  - Adopt green procurement requirements in line with government guidelines.  - Promote more environmentally sustainable practices across the financial sector and the broader community.  - Build a dynamic workforce and talent pool to support the HKMA's strategic objectives.  - Foster a collaborative, caring, and inclusive work environment that values diversity and strengthens employees' sense of belonging.  - Provide a high-quality working environment that supports healthy lifestyles.  - Cultivate a culture of social responsibility.  - Integrate social considerations into procurement processes and supply chain management.  - Advance financial inclusion and enhance the public's financial literacy through consumer education initiatives.  The HKMA is committed to addressing climate change and leading by example. In October 2024, the Monetary Authority announced that it would accelerate its target to achieve net-zero emissions from its own operations to 2030, two decades earlier than its original commitment, as part of its Action Plan. The Monetary Authority has updated its roadmap for the transition to net zero, with a focus on responsibly managing the environmental impact of daily operations. Key priorities include reducing carbon emissions, improving energy efficiency, cutting paper usage, and promoting waste recycling, while fully leveraging improvements in the fuel mix adopted by local power generators. In addition, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority has established a digital working environment to enhance efficiency while simultaneously reducing its carbon footprint. Furthermore, recognizing the importance of cultivating a culture of sustainability, the Monetary Authority actively encourages staff to adopt sustainable practices through ongoing promotional initiatives and activities. In alignment with the primary 2030 net-zero target, the HKMA has been exploring the adoption of carbon-embedded tools within its own value chain to reduce emissions and pursue low-carbon procurement to the greatest extent possible. In this regard, since 2023, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has fully offset the carbon emissions from its air travel by purchasing sustainable aviation fuel and participating in carbon offset programs. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will expand its Carbon Embedded and Carbon Offset schemes to cover all remaining major carbon emissions. In addition to the environmental commitments related to actual operations outlined above, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority continues to drive the market's transition to a low-carbon economy, ranging from the introduction of electronic document submission and processing procedures to promoting electronic payments and facilitating the return of coins to circulation. The remainder of this chapter details the Monetary Authority's strategies for leading in environmental sustainability, promoting employee well-being, and caring for society. Within the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's (HKMA) overarching institutional risk management framework, the Risk Committee, chaired by the HKMA Chief Executive, is responsible for monitoring and reviewing potential risks and threats arising from the HKMA's day-to-day operations, including those linked to climate change. To more effectively assess the potential impact of climate change on operations, the Monetary Authority has identified various climate-related risks and examined their actual and potential impacts. To address climate-related risks while ensuring continuous operations, the HKMA's offices have incorporated multiple measures to mitigate potential physical hazards, fires, and other emergencies. In addition, the Monetary Authority regularly updates its contingency plans, incorporating comprehensive measures that cover not only the offices but also communication and computer facilities. The Monetary Authority of Singapore regularly conducts evacuation and contingency facility activation drills to ensure that staff are always prepared to implement emergency response measures. The Monetary Authority has consistently monitored transition risks by tracking its own greenhouse gas emissions, waste generation, energy consumption, and paper usage. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's latest climate goal is to achieve net zero greenhouse gas emissions associated with its operations, covering Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3, by 2030 or earlier. These targets were established in reference to the methodology of the Science Based Targets initiative (SBTi). The Monetary Authority adopts the Greenhouse Gas Protocol to measure and report institutional emissions. Scope 1 emissions are direct emissions from gasoline vehicles. Given its operational nature, the majority of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's greenhouse gas emissions stem from Scope 2 indirect emissions resulting from the consumption of fossil fuels for electricity generation. In the absence of supplier-specific data, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) adopted a conservative approach to estimate Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions associated with purchased goods and services, including capital goods. Other Scope 3 emissions include waste sent to landfills, as well as employee business air travel and commuting. Detailed calculation results for 2023 and 2024 are provided in the "Performance Summary" on page 50. The performance data disclosed by the Monetary Authority has been independently verified by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency. The scope and criteria for the assurance provided by the Bureau are set out in the accompanying "Assurance Statement" at the end of this report. The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) leads by example, adhering to the same climate-related standards that it expects its regulated banks and the broader financial system under its supervision to follow. As a first step toward green transportation, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) began replacing its gasoline-powered vehicles with electric vehicles in 2024 and will continue this initiative in 2025 to achieve comprehensive green mobility. The Monetary Authority of Singapore continues to integrate environmental considerations into the design, operations, and maintenance of its premises. Specifically, as part of its 2024 renovation projects, the HKMA reutilized existing furniture and interior finishes, or exchanged used items for new ones at a discounted rate, thereby reducing waste. To enhance overall energy efficiency, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) regularly reviews energy consumption and energy-saving measures in its offices and data centres. As part of its 2024 data centre facility upgrade, the HKMA adopted a modular design for its uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, further optimising the Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) of its Green Building Council (HKBEAM) certified data centre. This design offers flexible capacity expansion, improved operating efficiency at partial loads, and incorporates advanced refrigeration technology with higher power density, thereby helping to reduce overall energy consumption. The Monetary Authority has enhanced internal virtual collaboration through its Digital Workspace, complemented by streamlined workflows, effectively reducing paper consumption. Furthermore, by aligning the lifespan of mobile and desktop devices with manufacturers' software update cycles, the HKMA can extend their period of secure usage. To minimize office-generated waste, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong (MAH) adheres to the "4R" principle—refuse, reduce, reuse, and recycle—and conducts regular waste audits to inform the development of targeted waste management strategies. The Monetary Authority has placed recycling bins at several convenient locations throughout its offices to collect various recyclable materials. To enhance recycling rates, the Monetary Authority established dedicated recycling bins for beverage cartons and plastic fruit mesh bags in 2024. Furthermore, since November 2022, the Monetary Authority has been sending collected food waste to a waste-to-energy facility in Hong Kong. In May 2024, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong joined the Environmental Protection Department's "Commitment to Waste Reduction in Activities," pledging to implement measures to reduce waste generated by its operations. The Monetary Authority of Singapore continues to prioritize the procurement of goods that meet the environmental specifications outlined in the Government's Green Procurement List, particularly electrical appliances and office consumables. To reduce carbon emissions from air travel, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority encourages employees to carefully plan their itineraries, such as consolidating multiple trips when attending overseas events. At the institutional level, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) has purchased sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) since 2023, reducing its annual aviation travel carbon emissions by approximately 10%. In addition, the HKMA participated in a Gold Standard-certified carbon offset program to neutralize the remaining carbon emissions from air travel; the program focuses on renewable energy production and electrification projects in emerging markets. In 2024, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) organized a range of learning activities for its staff, including lectures and guided tours of its waste-to-energy facility, to enhance employees' understanding of environmental sustainability issues. The Monetary Authority of Singapore will host its inaugural "MAS Green Month" from Earth Day on April 22, 2024, throughout the entire month of May, under the theme "Green Thinking, Green Living, Green Working." This presents a valuable opportunity to reaffirm the HKMA's commitment and drive to advance the sustainability of its internal operational practices. The event featured a "Sustainable Living BINGO Card" to encourage staff to adopt green lifestyles, a "Save the Earth" quiz, and a Japanese-inspired "Kokedama" indoor plant care workshop. It also included a presentation of waste audit findings and an overview of best practices in recycling by operators of the community recycling centre. To sustain the momentum of "Green Month," the HKMA launched a six-month collection campaign in October, emphasizing responsible waste management and reminding staff that small individual habit changes can significantly enhance the organization's overall recycling performance. A highlight of the event was the launch of the "Green Fit Action" video series, featuring senior executives sharing practical recycling tips. The initiative also launched a suite of screen savers, eye-catching posters, intranet articles, and digital reminders to encourage employees to actively reduce waste and increase recycling. In late 2024, the Monetary Authority of Hong Kong conducted a staff survey to gauge employees' understanding of sustainability and to gather their feedback on proposed green office initiatives. The findings will inform the future development of sustainable training programs and waste management strategies. As Hong Kong's central banking authority, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority sees itself as a key driver of change, committed to leading the acceleration of the low-carbon transition and promoting sustainable practices across the financial sector and society at large. The Monetary Authority has introduced multiple measures to enhance the efficiency of external processes. Following the successful launch of the Shared Data Submission Platform in 2023, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) will expand the platform's scope in 2024 to include non-bank institutions, such as stored-value payment facility operators, to facilitate their submission of certain regulatory data. The objective of expanding the platform's service scope is to further streamline the submission process for reporting institutions, provide a smoother experience for all users, and reinforce the HKMA's commitment to sustainability. Other new measures launched in 2024 include SurveyTool, which enables banks to respond to the Hong Kong Monetary Authority's questionnaire through a streamlined submission process, and an intelligent information and document management system that provides a centralized platform offering advanced search capabilities and bank-related document management features for users.

The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency has independently verified the environmental data (the "Data") of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority ("the Authority"). The data include 2024 total energy consumption, Scope 1 and Scope 2 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, paper usage, non-hazardous waste generated (comprising general waste and recyclables sent to landfills), and GHG emissions from air travel, along with their respective intensity metrics. Furthermore, the data include Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions from purchased goods and services, capital goods, fuel- and energy-related activities, non-hazardous waste (including general waste and recyclable waste sent to landfills), and employee commuting for 2023 and 2024, along with their corresponding emission intensities. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority's greenhouse gas emission data have been prepared in accordance with the Greenhouse Gas Protocol, a joint initiative of the World Resources Institute and the World Business Council for Sustainable Development. The scope of verification covers assets across six office and warehouse locations: five offices situated at 1) Two International Finance Centre, 2) Hopewell Centre, 3) Taikoo Place Phase I, 4) Kowloon Trade Centre, and 5) International Commerce Centre; and one warehouse located at 6) Lee Shing Industrial Centre in Kwai Chung. The purpose of validation is to provide reasonable assurance of the accuracy and reliability of data, and to confirm the adequacy of the data collection mechanisms of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority. Within the scope of verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority reviewed representative data and supporting evidence selected from six assets. This verification engagement was conducted in accordance with International Standard on Assurance Engagements 3000 (Revised), "Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information," issued by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board. The verification process is designed to provide an opinion and conclusion that yields a reasonable level of assurance. The verification process is conducted in accordance with the requirements of the GHG Protocol. The verification process tested the completeness and accuracy of the selected sample data by tracing it back to its source. It also reviewed the fundamental procedures for data collection, aggregation, estimation, calculation, and internal controls, and conducted reliability testing. The verification process also includes validating internal data collection and management mechanisms, conducting interviews with representatives responsible for preparing the data, and selecting representative data and information for verification. The underlying raw data and supporting evidence were also thoroughly reviewed during the validation process. The Monetary Authority is responsible for data collection and reporting. Our verification work is conducted with absolute independence and impartiality. The Hong Kong Quality Assurance Authority verification team did not participate in the data preparation process. Based on the results of this verification, the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency provides reasonable assurance regarding the data and concludes that: - the data are substantially accurate and reliable; and - the overall data collection mechanism of the Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau is adequate. Shen Xiaoyin was reviewed by the Hong Kong Quality Assurance Agency in March 2025.
